name: WatermelonDB
tagline: Lazy-loading reactive database for React Native and React apps, built on SQLite.
description: WatermelonDB is an observable, lazily loaded database layer for React Native and web apps, built by Nozbe for their task manager. On mobile it stores data in SQLite through a native bridge (JSI on modern React Native), and on the web it falls back to LokiJS over IndexedDB. Records load only when a component needs them, so apps with tens of thousands of rows still start quickly. It ships a sync protocol (pull/push of changes since a timestamp) but leaves the server side to you. Releases have slowed since 0.28 in 2025.

scale.notes: Comfortable with tens of thousands of records per device thanks to lazy loading.

strengths: Lazy loading keeps React Native app start-up fast with large local datasets
Observable queries re-render React components automatically
SQLite under the hood on iOS and Android, accessed via JSI
Simple, documented sync protocol that works with any backend
weaknesses: You must implement the sync server endpoints and conflict policy yourself
Slow release cadence and a shrinking core maintainer pool
Web adapter relies on LokiJS, which is itself unmaintained
useCases: Apps with large local lists that must render instantly
Custom sync to an existing REST backend
notIdealFor: Web-first apps (the web adapter is the weak spot)
